---
title: "7 · Quantum Machine Learning"
---

The tutorial closes where randomness becomes a *liability*. The expressivity that
makes deep quantum circuits interesting is exactly what makes them hard to train, 
and the proof is the Haar second moment from Chapter 3.

The central phenomenon is the **barren plateau**: for a circuit that is random
enough to form a 2-design, the variance of any cost-function gradient vanishes
**exponentially** in the number of qubits. The optimization landscape flattens, and
gradient-based training stalls. The same calculation explains the cures, 
**local** cost functions, symmetry restrictions, shallow blocks, which keep the
circuit *away* from full Haar randomness and restore a polynomial gradient.

The plateau wears several faces, all the same physics:

- **quantum kernels** whose entries concentrate exponentially, washing out the
 similarity structure a kernel method needs;
- **quantum Fisher information** that flattens, the metrology-flavored view of the
 same variance collapse;
- **generative and reservoir models** (Born machines, extreme learning machines,
 reservoir computing) where over-scrambling pushes outputs toward
 Porter-Thomas statistics and useful signal concentrates away.

The lesson is a balance. Scrambling buys expressivity but costs trainability, and
the useful regime is the structured, *incomplete* one in between.

## Notebooks in this part

- [Barren plateaus](../notebooks/ch7/solution_ch7_barren_plateau.ipynb), gradient variance vanishing exponentially with qubit number.
- [Local vs global cost functions](../notebooks/ch7/solution_ch7_local_vs_global_cost.ipynb), how observable locality rescues trainability.
- [Barren plateaus via quantum Fisher information](../notebooks/ch7/solution_ch7_barren_plateau_quantum_fisher_information.ipynb), the metrology view of the same collapse.
- [Quantum kernel concentration](../notebooks/ch7/solution_ch7_quantum_kernel_concentration.ipynb), why over-expressive kernels become uninformative.
- [Born-machine expressivity](../notebooks/ch7/solution_ch7_born_machine.ipynb), concentration of a generative model's output distribution.
- [QELM feature concentration](../notebooks/ch7/solution_ch7_quantum_extreme_learning_machine_concentration.ipynb), feature collapse in quantum extreme learning machines.
- [Quantum reservoir computing](../notebooks/ch7/solution_ch7_quantum_reservoir_computing_injection.ipynb), injection contractivity and restarting overhead.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Full circle.** The exponential that obstructs training here is the same
$1/D$ from the Page formula in Chapter 3, typicality, viewed from the other side.
:::
